# ambercast

> Prompt-native end-to-end testing.

## START HERE
- [Why I built ambercast](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/introduction/): The story of how I went from hating manual click-through testing to turning AI-driven click-through testing into an asset.
- [Philosophy](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/philosophy/): The design decisions that follow from treating tests as assets, laid out in the order they build on each other.
- [How it works](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-it-works/): Follow generate, run, and heal through three files and three commands, using login.test.md as the example.

## TUTORIALS
- [Your first test in 5 minutes](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/tutorials/quick-start/): Initialize a project, then generate, replay, and confirm your first generated test in this tutorial.
- [Reading your first plan and grounding](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/tutorials/review-your-first-plan/): Find the plan and grounding files ambercast generated, and read their freshness from a check result.
- [Healing a test after a UI change](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/tutorials/repair-your-first-drift/): Change the UI of a disposable practice app, then repair the failing test with an idempotent target.
- [Running ambercast in GitHub Actions](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/tutorials/github-actions/): Add two lines to a working GitHub Actions job so that run starts only after check passes.

## HOW-TO GUIDES
- [Write effective prompts](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/write-effective-prompts/): Write a focused test prompt, preview generation with --dry-run, and then generate.
- [Manage secrets](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/manage-secrets/): Approve the secret names that generation proposes and pass their values through environment variables.
- [Configure targets](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/configure-targets/): Write targets in the configuration file, then add heal isolation, an element wait, and secret sink origins.
- [Choose an AI provider](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/choose-ai-provider/): Pin a provider in configuration, let auto choose one, or override the provider for a single command.
- [Select which tests run](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/select-tests/): Four ways to choose which test prompts run, by path, pattern filter, or config exclusion.
- [Control grounding write-back](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/control-grounding-writeback/): Decide whether changed grounding is written back locally and in CI.
- [Review generated diffs](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/review-generated-diffs/): After generate or heal, list every changed file and read the prompt, plan, and grounding in order.
- [Manage artifacts in git](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/manage-artifacts-in-git/): Commit the prompt, plan, and grounding together and ignore the run evidence.
- [Run on other CI platforms](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/run-on-other-ci/): Run check and then run on GitLab CI or a generic runner, with healing left off.
- [Recover stale artifacts](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/recover-stale-artifacts/): Resolve stale, missing, or orphaned artifacts based on their check status.
- [Upgrade between versions](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/upgrade/): Upgrade ambercast, regenerate stale plans, and commit them with the dependency.
- [Troubleshoot common failures](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/troubleshoot/): Find the action for an observed symptom and re-run the smallest affected command.
- [Contribute](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/contribute/): Submit a change by issue, fork, three checks, and pull request, or report a vulnerability.

## REFERENCE
- [Configuration](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/configuration/): Configuration keys, defaults, and the rules for choosing a configuration file in ambercast.
- [Prompt file format](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/prompt-format/): Which files ambercast treats as test prompts, how it normalizes them, and how prompts and plans handle secret references.
- [Discovery patterns](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/discovery-patterns/): Pattern grammar, selection stages, defaults, and ordering that decide which test prompts ambercast discovers.
- [Reports](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/reports/): Report envelope, per-command result shapes, error details, and persistence rules for ambercast structured JSON reports.
- [Error codes](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/error-codes/): Stable error codes with their kind, scope, and exit code, and what each code's details contain.
- [Exit codes](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/exit-codes/): Process exit codes that ambercast returns, and the priority order that combines several outcomes into one code.
- [Environment variables](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/environment-variables/): Environment variables that ambercast reads, and the variables it withholds from AI-provider child processes.
- [File layout](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/file-layout/): Reference for the paths Ambercast derives for companion files and run artifacts, who writes each one, and when.
- [JSON Schemas](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/json-schemas/): Publication metadata, generated files, and structural limits of the JSON Schemas for Ambercast configuration, plan, grounding, and report documents.
- [Compatibility](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/compatibility/): Artifact-format compatibility across package versions, and the changes that require you to regenerate a Plan, Grounding, or report.
- [Changelog](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/changelog/): User-visible product behavior and public-contract changes across ambercast releases, with breaking changes listed first.
- [Security policy](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/security-policy/): Which ambercast versions receive security fixes, and how to report a vulnerability privately.
- [Glossary](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/glossary/): The normative site-wide terms of Ambercast and the index of literal tokens that translators keep verbatim.
- [MCP Tools](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/mcp-tools/): Tool contracts, inputs, results, and errors for ambercast MCP workflows.

### CLI
- [CLI overview](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/overview/): The seven ambercast commands, the options each command accepts, and the file discovery defaults.
- [ambercast generate](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/generate/): Flags, provider resolution, secret consent, companion files, and exit statuses of ambercast generate.
- [ambercast run](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/run/): Reference for the ambercast run command, covering CLI flags, replay paths, explicit AI resolution, grounding write-back, and report persistence.
- [ambercast check](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/check/): Flags, status values, result fields, and the read-only contract of ambercast check, which inspects plan and grounding freshness.
- [ambercast heal](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/heal/): Flags, repair stages, limits, authorization, CI rule, and write behavior of ambercast heal.
- [ambercast init](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/init/): Synopsis, flags, written files, confirmation, and exit codes of ambercast init, which scaffolds a configuration file, a sample prompt, and repository guidance.
- [ambercast view](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/view/): Flags, the interactive gate, port selection, host binding, and served routes of ambercast view.
- [ambercast mcp](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/mcp/): Launch, transport, lifecycle, and client registration for the MCP server.

## PLAN SPECIFICATION
- [Ambercast Plan Specification](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/overview/): This specification describes the artifacts accepted by ambercast 0.10.0.
- [Plan document](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/plan-document/): This chapter defines `PlanDocument`, the committed plan file's top-level object, its minimal example, and the generation response that local generation turns into it.
- [Steps](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/steps/): This chapter defines every committed step kind, its fields and example, and the generated forms that local generation turns into committed steps.
- [Value types](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/value-types/): This chapter defines the shared objects and scalar contracts that the other chapters reference by name.
- [Grounding document](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/grounding-document/): This chapter defines `GroundingDocument`, the committed grounding cache bound to one plan digest, its entries and trace records, and when an implementation writes or keeps an entry.
- [Element fingerprint](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/fingerprint/): This chapter defines the element fingerprint that grounding stores for an element step, how the fingerprint is computed, and how a stored fingerprint is matched.
- [Freshness and digests](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/freshness/): This chapter defines `inputsDigest` and `planDigest`, which decide whether a plan and its grounding are current, and the `check` statuses derived from them.
- [Canonical JSON](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/canonical-json/): This chapter defines the compact digest form, the indented artifact form, and the atomic-visibility contract for storage writes.
- [Secrets in plans](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/secrets/): This chapter defines how plans refer to secrets, how secret names are authorized, where resolved values can be sent, and how literal secrets are rejected.
- [Conformance](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/conformance/): This chapter defines what a conforming validator checks: the JSON Schema projections, the semantic constraints with their issue codes, and the verification order.
- [Specification changelog](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/changelog/): Artifact version acceptance MUST follow Ambercast Plan Specification, not release-number intuition.

## EXPLANATION
- [Plan lifecycle and freshness](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/plan-lifecycle/): A plan can be replayed only while it matches the inputs that produced it, and `check` decides that without running anything.
- [Replay and grounding](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/replay-and-grounding/): Replay reuses recorded grounding, so a fully covered run needs no AI call, and a miss either fails closed or is resolved live only with `--resolve`.
- [Healing model](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/healing-model/): Explains how far ambercast repairs a test automatically when a UI change breaks it, and where it hands off to your judgment.
- [Trust and security](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/trust-and-security/): ambercast trusts only what it has validated locally, and page content, provider output, and secret values each cross a boundary that fails closed.
- [Determinism in CI](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/determinism-in-ci/): In CI, ambercast inspects without side effects, writes only the run report and contained evidence by default, refuses to repair by default, and reports one exit code.
- [How ambercast compares](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/comparison/): ambercast keeps the natural-language prompt as the test and derives a reviewed plan from it, while other models keep a script or a live session.
- [Status and roadmap](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/status-and-roadmap/): What the current release implements, what is planned, and how versions move before 1.0.

## FOR AI AGENTS
- [Using ambercast from an AI agent](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/overview/): Before an agent changes a test asset it reads four pages in order, then works in a loop of implement, write the prompt, run, and fix from the report.
- [Operating contract](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/): For each command, this page says what must hold before you run it, what it may write, whether it needs the user's approval, and what to do after an exit code or report error.
- [Setup prompt](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/setup-prompt/): Paste this prompt into a coding agent so it works only on the requested test, presents a diff, and asks before any write it was not asked for.
- [Reading structured output](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/reading-structured-output/): Read a JSON report in a fixed order, `command`, then `reportPersistence` for `run`, then `errors[].code`, then each `results[].status`, and act on the first that calls for it.
- [Machine-readable resources](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/machine-readable-resources/): The site publishes these machine-readable files, and `capabilities.json` decides which of them are available.
- [Official skill](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/official-skill/): ambercast ships an Agent Skills skill named `ambercast` that teaches a coding agent the prompt, run, and report loop, and this page says what it covers and where it sits next to the setup prompt and the MCP server.
- [MCP server](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/mcp-server/): `ambercast mcp` serves one session root over stdio to an MCP client, and this page says what the agent can call and where each call's details live.
